decision.user_intent: Every JANUS device is an independent compute node that can operate fully solo or communicate with peers. Together they form a swarm. More healthy nodes mean more observations, more exchanged experience, and potentially better collective learning because the swarm sees a larger and more diverse data surface.

swarm_contract.topology: peer swarm with role specialization; no single node is required to be the whole JANUS
swarm_contract.benefit_hypothesis: Increasing the number and diversity of healthy nodes should increase useful data and model diversity, but improvement must be measured rather than assumed.
anti_failure_rules: one noisy/bad node must not poison all peers
peer identity and provenance are preserved

learning_architecture.local: each node learns from its own real stream and local outcomes
learning_architecture.collective: nodes exchange bounded experience/model summaries and can learn from peer outcomes
learning_architecture.habitat: NAS/PC is an optional heavy-compute/archive/replay/distillation organ, not a mandatory brain; nodes must remain useful without it
learning_architecture.promotion: peer/global candidate knowledge is shadow-tested locally before promotion where feasible

sha256_parallel_lane.role: A parallel compute/learning lane: the swarm can quietly process Buzz-assigned SHA-256/Stratum work while preserving the protocol's exact mathematical truth.
success_metrics: best bits / best difficulty where meaningful

zim_status.statement: User reports Zim currently shows the best practical success among current swarm learning/mining nodes.
zim_status.action: Preserve Zim as the current lead candidate/model donor, but do not promote the claim to measured best until logs are replayed under a frozen comparison protocol.
